question: Does a conditional generative model (flow matching with a stochastic interpolant, same backbone and budget as R1-R6) give calibrated range-error distributions, does its SPR mean do better than the regression Bayes act R3, and does it estimate range-error tails better than the R6 head?

model.interpolant: x_t = (1 - t) x_0 + t x_1 + gamma(t) z, gamma(t) = 2 eta t (1 - t), in encoded CT units
model.x0: bulk-density image of the body (0 HU inside, -1000 HU outside)
model.outputs: drift E[x_1 - x_0 + gamma'(t) z | x_t] and, for eta > 0, denoiser E[z | x_t]
model.sampler: Euler-Maruyama, eps(t) = kappa gamma(t), kappa = 0.1 (injected noise of the order of the interpolant noise), from X_0 = x_0
model.backbone: TimeUNet2d: the U-Net of the regression arms (same widths and depth) with FiLM time conditioning
model.point_prediction: SPR mean of the samples, g^-1(mean_k g(sample_k)) (Proposition 4)

subsets.rule: region-stratified, hashed order within region (sctrange.dosimetry.select_cases); development cases with a seed-0 R3 prediction

sweep.selection_rule: among eta > 0, the lowest median over the sweep cases; ties go to the smaller eta. eta = 0 is deterministic and serves as the collapse control, never as a candidate

comparators: R3 and R6 of the S4 runs, seed 0 (same single-seed budget as the generator), on the main cases

collapse.statement: eta = 0 is deterministic: its median ensemble spread must be at most 5 % of the smallest median spread among eta > 0

calibration.coverage: share of rays whose true WET lies in the central 90 % interval of the ensemble (nominal 0.9)
calibration.pit: rank of the truth among the samples, pooled over rays; uniform when calibrated
calibration.uncertainty_error: per-case Spearman between ensemble spread and absolute WET error of the point prediction; median reported

notes: Projected CRPS is proper but not strictly proper on finite segment families (docs/theory.md, Proposition 8).
risk_fz compares each model's tail forecast with its own error; the outcomes differ between G and R6, so risk_miscalibration (|coverage - 0.9|) is reported alongside.
The theory predicts that the generator's mean equals R3 at best; a significant gain would point to a better-fitted model rather than to the generative formulation.
